what: The score maximizes the distance saved by inserting the customer into the current route rather than serving it by a separate depot round trip. That saving is multiplied by a modest factor based on the fraction of current remaining capacity consumed. Runtime is O(len(route)) for computing the current load, with O(1) extra memory.
why: Depot-trip savings favors customers that are both far from the depot and geometrically compatible with the current route, encouraging compact route clusters under the farthest-customer seeding policy. The bounded capacity factor mildly prioritizes large, currently feasible demands—useful when heterogeneous demands might become difficult to pack later—without rewarding candidates that have no geometric saving. This is a construction surrogate rather than a remaining-cost estimate. It cannot anticipate later routes, RCL randomness, combinatorial bin-packing effects, or all improvements obtainable by 2-opt, and no empirical performance claim is implied.
